 The Tulsa Golden Hurricane (4-4) hit the road for an AAC battle against the Tulane Green Wave (4-4) on Saturday, November 7, 2026 at Yulman Stadium.
 You’ll want to check out ESPNU for the upcoming game between the Golden Hurricane and Green Wave.
 Watch Tulsa vs. Tulane with Fubo! 
 When is Tulsa vs. Tulane and when does it start? 
 This matchup between the Golden Hurricane and Green Wave will take place on Saturday, November 7, 2026. You should expect the kickoff at 12 p.m. ET.
 Where to watch Tulsa vs. Tulane 
 The Golden Hurricane and Green Wave will hit the gridiron at Yulman Stadium for this matchup on Nov. 7, and if you would like to see the game live, get your tickets now from Vivid Seats !
 What channel is the game on? 
 You can catch Tulsa vs. Tulane live on ESPNU. Watch the game live without cable on Fubo .

 Live Stream Online: Sign up for Fubo today! 
 Tulsa vs. Tulane Game Preview 
 Tulsa Stats & Insights
 In their most recent outing, the Golden Hurricane lost 38-35 to the Army Black Knights.
 Tulsa is putting up 369.8 yards per game on offense, which ranks 79th in the FBS. Defensively, the Golden Hurricane rank 113th, allowing 405.4 yards per game. 
 The Golden Hurricane are averaging 211.6 passing yards per game on offense, which ranks them 85th in the FBS. On defense, they rank 53rd, giving up 203.4 passing yards per contest. 
 Tulsa has the 65th-ranked rushing offense this season (158.1 rushing yards per game), and has been less effective on the other side of the ball, ranking ninth-worst with 202.0 rushing yards allowed per game.
 The Golden Hurricane are averaging 29.8 points per game offensively this year (57th in the FBS), and they are giving up 24.4 points per game (68th) on the other side of the ball.
 Tulane Stats & Insights
 Last time out, the Green Wave knocked off the Charlotte 49ers 38-31.
 Tulane ranks 104th in total yards per game (348.9), but it has been worse on the defensive side of the ball, ranking 14th-worst in the FBS with 421.9 total yards surrendered per contest.
 The Green Wave rank 98th in the FBS with 203.4 passing yards per contest on offense, and they rank 59th with 207.6 passing yards given up per contest on defense.
 Tulane has been struggling in run defense, ranking seventh-worst with 214.3 rushing yards surrendered per game. It has been better offensively, generating 145.5 rushing yards per contest (89th-ranked). 
 In terms of points scored the Green Wave rank 107th in the FBS (22.5 points per game), and they are 81st on the other side of the ball (25.4 points allowed per contest).
 Tulsa Key Players to Watch
 Baylor Hayes has thrown for 1,343 yards (223.8 ypg) to lead Tulsa, completing 63% of his passes and tossing 10 touchdown passes and two interceptions this season. He’s also contributed in the ground game with 70 rushing yards (11.7 ypg) on 35 carries with two rushing touchdowns.
 Damari Alston’s team-high 429 rushing yards (53.6 per game) have come on 103 carries, with six touchdowns this year. He’s also added 15 catches for 108 yards (15.4 per game).
 This season Trequan Jones has piled up 60 carries for 388 yards (48.5 per game) and four touchdowns.
 Oran Singleton’s 535 receiving yards (66.9 yards per game) lead the team. He has 43 receptions with four touchdowns.
 Javon Ross has collected 327 receiving yards (40.9 yards per game) and three touchdowns, hauling in 28 passes this year.
 Jimmy Calloway’s 23 receptions are good enough for 215 yards (43.0 ypg) and one touchdown.
 Tulane Key Players to Watch
 Kadin Semonza has 804 passing yards (160.8 ypg) to lead Tulane, completing 53.8% of his passes and collecting four touchdown passes and two interceptions this season.
 Johnnie Daniels’ team-high 493 rushing yards (61.6 per game) have come on 79 carries, with six touchdowns this year.
 This season Maurice Turner has racked up 341 yards (56.8 per game) on 43 carries with two touchdowns, while also catching six passes for 96 yards (19.2 per game) and one touchdown.
 Destyn Hill’s 390 receiving yards (48.8 yards per game) lead the team. He has 32 receptions with two touchdowns.
 Anthony Brown has reeled in 23 passes for 277 yards (34.6 yards per game) and one touchdown this year.
 Bredell Richardson’s 15 catches have yielded 153 yards (19.1 ypg).
